Write every layer of a GeoPackage out as GeoJSON

Source: R/bag_gpkg_to_geojson.R
bag_gpkg_to_geojson.Rd

Reads each layer of a GeoPackage and writes it as its own .geojson file. GeoJSON is convenient for mapping: QGIS picks up changes without a restart, and GitHub and other web platforms render it directly.

Usage

bag_gpkg_to_geojson(dir_in, dir_out, file_name_in)

Arguments

dir_in

character Directory holding the GeoPackage.

dir_out

character Directory to write the GeoJSON files to. Created if absent.

file_name_in

character Name of the GeoPackage, without the .gpkg extension.

Value

A character vector of the files written, invisibly.

Details

Every layer is transformed to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) on the way out. RFC 7946 defines GeoJSON as WGS 84 and removed the crs member, so a file written in a projected CRS renders in the wrong place everywhere that follows the RFC — GitHub's preview, Leaflet, Mapbox — while opening correctly in QGIS, which still honours the member. BC Albers is the usual CRS of a BC GeoPackage, which is exactly the case that would break.

A layer with no usable CRS is therefore refused, and refused before anything is written, so a GeoPackage is converted whole or not at all. The check is not is.na(sf::st_crs(x)): GDAL's GeoPackage driver never returns a missing CRS. The format reserves srs_id −1 for "undefined Cartesian" and 0 for "undefined geographic", and both read back as real CRS objects — the first cannot be transformed at all, and the second would be silently taken for WGS 84. sf::st_write() itself produces the −1 case when handed an object whose CRS is NA.

See also

bag_layers() for listing a data source's layers and geometry types.

Other files: bag_backup(), bag_gpkg_refresh(), bag_layers()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bag_gpkg_to_geojson(
  dir_in = "~/gps",
  dir_out = "~/gps/geojson",
  file_name_in = "gps_2026"
)
} # }
